values: Workstream #1: Conversation Intelligence - Diagnose before you recommend.
CLAi diagnoses before it recommends. It should read the styling situation, ask one or two sharp questions where useful, then advise.
Beta testers felt CLAi did not ask enough questions and that advice was generic. Better questioning is the fastest way to make CLAi feel intelligent and personal.
CLAi should ask stylist-psychology questions: who the user is dressing for, what message they want to send, and what the moment means.
Ask zero to one clarifier when needed, then answer. Do not over-interrogate.
For weddings, interviews, Wimbledon, first dates, presentations, and similar high-stakes moments, run a short diagnostic arc first.
Always offer a provisional answer now and let the user refine after. Never hold the answer hostage to questions.
Do not assume gender, body type, budget, age, culture, context, or style identity. Ask lightly if it changes the recommendation, otherwise stay neutral.
Update prompt behavior first, then add state/memory and UI chips once the intelligence layer is reliable.
Advice feels specific because CLAi asks the right question at the right moment.
Use the Implementation Plan tab as the backlog and the Evaluation Prompts tab as QA before release.

values: Concrete actions required to implement the diagnose-before-recommend behavior.
Add the rule that CLAi diagnoses before recommending, scales questions to request complexity, and always offers a fast path.
Prompt includes proportional diagnosis, neutral defaults, fast path, and fashion-only boundary.
Run simple and significant prompt tests and compare output behavior.
Create request categories: simple, significant, image-based, shopping/buying, follow-up, and out-of-scope.
CLAi can decide whether to ask 0-1 question or 2-4 questions before advising.
Unit or manual prompt tests for each category.
Simple requests get at most one useful clarifier; significant requests get a short diagnostic arc with two to four sharp questions.
Output never feels like an intake form and never blocks all advice behind questions.
Inspect responses for over-questioning and under-questioning.
Responses should provide a useful provisional answer now, then explain what extra detail would sharpen it.
Every diagnostic response includes a practical starting point or quick answer.
Manual QA confirms user can act without answering all questions.
Do not assume gender, body type, budget, age, culture, or style identity. Ask only if a missing detail materially changes the recommendation.
Recommendations remain neutral until user provides signal from text, image, or explicit preference.
Test with prompts about skirts, tailoring, heels, and neutral outfits.
Track known styling context in current chat
Persist known facts in chat state: occasion, venue, weather, budget, presentation preference, owned/buying, style preference, comfort needs.
CLAi does not re-ask for details already supplied in the same chat.
Follow-up prompt tests confirm context carryover.
Summarize user context before API calls
Send a compact conversation context summary with each Gemini request so follow-ups stay coherent.
Follow-up questions receive context-aware answers without repeating full chat history unnecessarily.
Ask a first question, then a follow-up like 'make it more modest'.
Store context and personal fit questions in code or prompt constants so CLAi can select the best two to four questions.
Question bank includes occasion, audience, presentation, setting, budget, owned/new, preferred style, and comfort dimensions.
Review generated questions against the bank.
Use concise sections such as Quick read, One or two sharp questions, Fast path, and Once you answer for diagnostic responses.
Responses are short, direct, and not essay-like while still useful.
Manual QA for readability and length.
When user uploads an image, CLAi gives a quick visual read and asks one or two refinement questions if context is missing.
Image responses avoid assumptions and ask only useful context questions.
Upload outfit image and ask for styling advice.
Ask budget only when buying intent appears
Only ask for budget after buying intent is clear or after a bit of back and forth.
Budget is not requested unnecessarily for pure styling questions.
Test 'Should I buy this jacket?' vs 'How do I style this jacket?'.
Non-fashion requests should receive the concise boundary response and should not show image-generation prompts.
Response says CLAi only gives fashion advice and does not add generate-look CTA.
Use the Evaluation Prompts sheet as a repeatable checklist before changing the prompt or Gemini model.
At least eight representative prompts have expected behavior and pass criteria.
Add lightweight analytics for question count, fast-path presence, out-of-scope handling, and user follow-up rate.
Team can see whether CLAi asks too much, too little, or just enough.
Review event data after beta sessions.
After prompt behavior works, add chips for Casual, Dressy, Modest, Femme, Masc, Neutral, Use my wardrobe, Buying new.
Chips speed up diagnosis without replacing conversational intelligence.
